newsitem.title: USA: US Mid-Atlantic power stabilizes after Tuesday drop.
newsitem.headline: US Mid-Atlantic power stabilizes after Tuesday drop.

text.p: Day-ahead electricity prices in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect pool stablized Wednesday after Tuesday's drop on mild temperatures across the Mid-Atlantic region.
Brokers and marketers said the daily market held steady on expectations that Thursday's energy demand would mirror today's.
"The weather is going to be the same or cooler tomorrow," said a PJM power marketer.

Forecasts showed temperatures in the Mid-Atlantic region would stay very mild, peaking in the high-40s to low-50s F range Thursday. A cool air mass would moderate readings toward seasonal norms this weekend into early this week.
Thursday PJM power for firm, peak delivery changed hands in a $22.00-22.50 per megawatt hour (MWh) range, compared with Tuesday's $21.50-23.00 for delivery today.
PJM day-ahead electricity for firm, off-peak delivery slipped to $17.00-18.00, down 50 cents from Tuesday.
The "split system" affecting PJM will continue Thursday despite moderate energy demand for the rest of the week, market sources said.
Weekday transmission capacity in the grid has been tight for the past couple of weeks due to high power flows into the eastern part of the system.
Peak production costs for Thursday in the western PJM held about $19.00, while rates in the east remained near $31.00.

Dispatch rates in the east are much higher because utilities have fired up expensive oil and natural gas plants to balance the grid, enabling them to bring in cheap, coal-fired generation from the west.
PJM electricity for delivery next week firmed in anticipation of cooler weather moving into the region, and was assessed 50 cents higher than Tuesday at $23.50-25.50.
Deferred PJM deliveries were flat to higher with a rebound in natural gas futures.
March PJM power prices rose to $23.60-23.95 from Tuesday's $23.40-23.65.
PJM prices for April and May tightened to $21.60-21.80 from $21.50-21.85 Tuesday, while June PJM power firmed to $24.50-24.75 from Tuesday's $24.40-24.70.
July/August PJM electricity climbed to $29.10-29.50 from $29.00-29.20 Tuesday.

Separately, natural gas prices recovered after faltering yesterday on the bearish short-term weather outlook. Swing deliveries at the Philadelphia city gate remained in the $2.10-2.20 per million British thermal unit (mmBtu) range.
At 1251 EST, NYMEX March Henry Hub gas futures were up 4.0 cents at $2.010/mmBtu.
